This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode) Perused the prisoner's petition dated 10.03.2023 in which the petitioner has requested to engage Mr. Biswajit Tripathy as his counsel.
Mr. Biswajit Tripathy is present in Court today and he filed his Vakalatnama, which is taken on record.
He also produced the certified copies of depositions of the victim and her husband who have been examined in the learned trial Court as P.W.7 and P.W.6 respectively.
The same are taken on record.
On perusal of the evidence of the victim, it appears that she has not supported the prosecution case.

This is an application under section 439 of Cr.P.C.
// 2 // in connection with Nimapara P.S. Case No.400 of 2021 corresponding to G.R. Case No.1067 of 2021 pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Nimapara for offences punishable under sections 363/376-D/323/294/354/354- B/379/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

The petitioner moved an application for bail before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge,
Nimapara, which was rejected on 05.03.2022.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 15.11.2021 and in the meantime, the victim has already been examined in the learned trial Court as P.W.7 and she has not supported the prosecution case and therefore, the bail application may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, since the victim has already been examined in the learned trial Court as P.W.7 who has not supported the prosecution case and taking into account the period of detention of the petitioner in judicial custody,
I am inclined to allow the prayer for bail and direct the petitioner to be released on bail.
Let the petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000.00 (rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties // 3 // each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter with further terms and conditions that the petitioner shall not try to keep any contact with the victim or any of the prosecution witnesses and he shall appear before the learned trial Court on each date to which the case is posted for trial.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge Sipun Bidyadhar Swain vs State Of Odisha ....
